svg.title: Prompting techniques: demonstrations and persona are separate choices
svg.desc: Two independent prompt comparisons use the same held-out architecture question: phone and browser clients need different tailored APIs. Panel A fixes the question, choices Bulkhead, API gateway, and BFF, and a label-only output format. Zero-shot has no worked question-answer examples, one-shot has one, and few-shot has three. These are alternatives, not steps; more examples do not guarantee a better answer. Panel B has no demonstrations in either prompt. Both ask for one trade-off in two short sentences; only the persona prompt adds: You are a cautious software architect. Consider operational cost. Shot count counts input-output demonstrations, not requests; zero-shot still contains instructions. A role instruction changes emphasis and does not guarantee expertise.

text.tspan: Examples and roles change different parts of a prompt
Two comparisons. Change one ingredient at a time.
A
Compare the number of worked examples
Keep the held-out question, choices, and output format identical.
Shared question
ShopEasy has phone and browser clients that need different tailored APIs. Which pattern fits?
Return exactly one label: Bulkhead, API gateway, or BFF.
Prompt variant
Worked Q → A examples included before that question
Zero-shot
0 examples
No worked question–answer pairs.
One-shot
1 example
Q: One external entry point applies routing and authentication. → A: API gateway
Few-shot
3 examples
Q: One external entry point applies routing and authentication. → A: API gateway
Q: Slow reporting exhausts a shared pool; isolate the resources. → A: Bulkhead
Q: A tablet app needs an API tailored to its screens. → A: BFF
These are alternatives, not stages. More examples do not guarantee a better answer.
B
Compare a neutral prompt with a persona
ShopEasy has phone and browser clients that need different tailored APIs. Which pattern fits?
Choices: Bulkhead · API gateway · BFF
Both prompts: choose a pattern and explain one trade-off in two short sentences.
Neutral · no role
No persona instruction is added.
Persona · one role
You are a cautious software architect.
Consider operational cost.
0 demonstrations in either prompt. Only the role instruction changes.
A persona can change emphasis; it does not guarantee expertise or correctness.
Zero-shot still has instructions. Shots count worked input → output demonstrations, not requests.
